message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • 55 mph on rural interstates
• 65 mph on urban interstates (unless posted otherwise)
• 45 mph on highways with 2–3 lanes per direction (unless posted)
• 35 mph on roads with 4+ lanes per direction (unless posted) | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.001‑545.004 | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts (except for certain motorcycle riders).
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 5 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % for drivers 21+.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers and drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑education programs, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.021‑545.023 | | **Reckless Driving** | • Driving with a willful or wanton disregard for safety.
• Penalties: up to 1 year in jail, fines up to $2,000, license suspension. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Running red lights, stop signs, or yielding incorrectly can lead to fines and points on your license. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.021‑545.023 | | **Points System & License Suspension** | • Accumulating 4 points in 12 months can lead to license suspension.
• Points are added for various infractions (speeding, DUI, reckless driving, etc.). | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) Rules** | • Separate set of rules for commercial vehicles (e.g., weight limits, hours of service).
• CDL holders face stricter penalties for DUI and other violations. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.021‑545.023 | | **Parking & Loading Zones** | • Parking restrictions vary by municipality; always check signage.
• Illegal parking can result in fines or towing. | Local ordinances, Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Roadway Safety Programs** | • Texas DOT runs programs like “Safe Driving” and “Vision Zero” to reduce crashes.
• Drivers can enroll in defensive‑driving courses for potential insurance discounts. | Texas Department of Transportation website | --- ### How to Stay Informed 1. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Official source for licensing, DUI enforcement, and traffic law updates. - Website: https://www.dps.texas.gov/ 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – The legal text governing all traffic laws. - Online: https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.545.htm 3. **Local County or City Ordinances** – Some rules (e.g., parking, speed limits on local roads) are set at the municipal level. - Check your city’s official website or contact the local police department. 4. **Legal Aid & Law Firms** – If you’re facing a traffic ticket or lawsuit, consult a Texas‑licensed attorney. - Texas Bar Association: https://www.texasbar.com/ --- ### Quick Tips for Texas Drivers - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they can change quickly, especially near construction zones. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. - **Keep your seat belt fastened** at all times. - **Check your vehicle’s registration and insurance** before hitting the road. - **If you’re pulled over**, remain calm, keep your hands visible, and comply with the officer’s instructions. Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detailed information on a specific area (e.g., DUI penalties, commercial driving regulations, or how to contest a ticket).
